propositions.text: Applicant seeks judicial review of Board decision dated December 17, 2014
propositions.quote: Mr. Ahmad Omid a.k.a. Omid Ahmad a.k.a. Farhad Ahmad Sultani (the “Applicant”) seeks judicial review of a decision of the Immigration and Refugee Board, Refugee Protection Division (the “Board”). In that decision, dated December 17, 2014, the Board determined that the Applicant is neither a Convention Refugee nor a person in need of protection pursuant to section 96 and subsection 97(1), respectively, of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c. 27.

propositions.text: Board decided Applicant is neither Convention Refugee nor person in need of protection under IRPA
propositions.quote: the Board determined that the Applicant is neither a Convention Refugee nor a person in need of protection pursuant to section 96 and subsection 97(1), respectively, of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c. 27.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant seeks judicial review of the Board's December 17, 2014 decision denying refugee or protection status.

propositions.text: Applicant is Afghan citizen who claimed protection based on social group, risk of cruel treatment, torture
propositions.quote: The Applicant is a citizen of Afghanistan. He sought protection in Canada on the basis of membership in a particular social group, risk to life or of cruel and usual treatment or punishment and danger of torture.

propositions.text: Board rejected claims due to lack of credibility, found Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) and presumption of state protection not rebutted
propositions.quote: The Board rejected his claims because it did not find the basis of his claim to be credible, and it found that the Applicant had an Internal Flight Alternative (“IFA”). The Board also found that the Applicant had failed to rebut the presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant is Afghan and the Board rejected his claims for credibility, IFA, and state protection reasons.

propositions.text: Three findings are reviewable on reasonableness standard per Tsyhanko and Dunsmuir
propositions.quote: These three findings are reviewable on the standard of reasonableness; see Tsyhanko v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship & Immigration), 2008 FC 819 at paragraphs 12-14. According to the decision in Dunsmuir v. New Brunswick, [2008] 1 S.C.R. 190, that standard requires that a decision be transparent, justifiable and intelligible.

propositions.text: Reasonableness standard allows range of acceptable decisions if transparent, justified, intelligible
propositions.quote: Application of the standard of reasonableness means that a range of possible, acceptable decisions is available to the decision maker, as long as the result meets the criteria of transparency, justification and intelligibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the reasonableness standard applies to three findings, requiring transparency, justification, and intelligibility.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness issues are reviewable on correctness standard per Khosa
propositions.quote: Issues of procedural fairness are reviewable on the standard of correctness; see the decision in Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v. Khosa, [2009] 1 S.C.R. 339 at paragraph 43.

paragraphs.summary: The court states procedural fairness issues are reviewed on the correctness standard per Khosa.

propositions.text: Court reviewed hearing transcript and parties' submissions
propositions.quote: I have reviewed the transcript of the hearing held before the Board on October 22, 2014. I have also considered the submissions of the parties

propositions.text: Respondent argues Applicant challenges weight given to evidence by Board
propositions.quote: agree with the argument of the Minister of Citizenship and Immigration (the “Respondent”) that essentially, the Applicant is challenging the weight given to the evidence by the Board.

paragraphs.summary: The court reviewed the hearing transcript and submissions, noting the Respondent says the Applicant challenges the Board's evidence weighting.

propositions.text: Court not persuaded Board's credibility findings are unreasonable under reasonableness standard
propositions.quote: I am not persuaded that the Board’s credibility findings are unreasonable, when measured against the standard of reasonableness referred to above.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board's credibility findings reasonable under the reasonableness standard.

propositions.text: No reviewable error in Board's findings on IFA and state protection; Board considered relevant principles and weighed evidence
propositions.quote: Likewise, I see no reviewable error in the manner in which the Board made its findings about an IFA and state protection. In each case, the Board considered the relevant principles and the relevant jurisprudence. The Board weighed the evidence before it, as it is authorized to do.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no error in the Board's IFA and state protection findings, which properly considered principles and evidence.

propositions.text: Considering evidence including country documents, Board's conclusions were reasonable and no judicial intervention warranted
propositions.quote: Considering the evidence that the Applicant put forward, including country condition documents, I am satisfied that the Board’s ultimate conclusions were reasonable and there is no basis for judicial intervention.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board's conclusions reasonable based on evidence and declines judicial intervention.

propositions.text: Applicant alleges Board breached procedural fairness by not considering second post-hearing submissions
propositions.quote: The Applicant submits that the Board breached his rights to procedural fairness by failing to consider the further post-hearing submissions and documents that were submitted on December 9, 2014.

propositions.text: Board accepted first post-hearing submissions but did not consider second set as it was functus
propositions.quote: Although the Board had accepted the first post-hearing submissions filed by the Applicant, it did not consider the second set of post-hearing materials, on the ground that it was functus.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant alleges procedural fairness breach for ignoring second post-hearing submissions; the Board accepted first but not second as functus.

propositions.text: Applicant's post-hearing submissions did not comply with Rule 43 of Refugee Protection Division Rules
propositions.quote: The Applicant in making his post-hearing submissions, including the presentation of further documents, did not comply with Rule 43 of the Refugee Protection Division Rules, SOR/2012-256.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Applicant's post-hearing submissions did not comply with Rule 43 of the Refugee Protection Division Rules.

propositions.text: Board was not obliged to consider non-compliant second submissions and did not breach procedural fairness
propositions.quote: The Board was not obliged to consider the second set of non-compliant submissions and evidence. It did not breach the procedural fairness rights owing to the Applicant.

propositions.text: No reviewable error in Board's refusal to consider second post-hearing submissions
propositions.quote: There is no reviewable error in this regard.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no breach of procedural fairness or reviewable error in the Board's refusal to consider non-compliant second submissions.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review dismissed with no question for certification
propositions.quote: In the result, this application for judicial review was dismissed, no question for certification arising. JUDGMENT THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that this application for judicial review was dismissed, no question for certification arising.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the judicial review application with no question for certification.
